validator-fix-3 (F3)

Compact review of the change from fix/val-doc-1 to task/validator-fix-3.

commit 14a8286 2 files +125 / −4 validator CLI
Contents TL;DR Per-file change Review verdict

TL;DR

getSentSnapshotData no longer assumes that the claim is calldata argument args[1]. It parses the called function’s fragment, finds the tuple-typed input, and hashes that decoded argument. This preserves the two-argument Arb→Eth case and fixes Arb→Gnosis, where args[1] is the gas limit and the claim is args[2].

Outcome
Both route ABIs are now exercised with their real TypeChain interfaces. The implementation satisfies the stated F3 acceptance criteria.

What changed, by file

validator-cli/src/utils/claim.ts

  • Added claimArgIndex(fragment). It walks the parsed fragment’s inputs from right to left and returns the first input whose baseType or type is tuple. It returns -1 when no tuple exists.
  • Replaced parsed.args[1]. getSentSnapshotData now uses the derived tuple index. This is the functional fix: Arb→Eth resolves index 1, while Arb→Gnosis resolves index 2.
  • Added safe null exits. A transaction that cannot be fetched, calldata that does not match the supplied interface, or a parsed fragment without a tuple now produces null.
  • Exported getSentSnapshotData. This permits direct unit testing; intent is inferred from the accompanying test import.
// Before: correct only for sendSnapshot(epoch, claim)
const claimTuple = parsed.args[1];

// After: derive the Claim position from the decoded ABI fragment
const index = claimArgIndex(parsed.fragment);
if (index === -1) return null;
const claimTuple = parsed.args[index] as unknown as ClaimStruct;

Why: on Arb→Gnosis, argument 1 is _gasLimit. Hashing it cannot match the outbox’s claim hash, so an already-sent snapshot remains classified as unsent.

validator-cli/src/utils/claim.test.ts

  • Imports the real VeaInboxArbToEth and VeaInboxArbToGnosis TypeChain factories rather than constructing test-only ABIs.
  • Encodes and checks both signatures: sendSnapshot(epoch, claim) and sendSnapshot(epoch, gasLimit, claim).
  • Proves the gas limit does not affect the derived claim hash and that changing the claim does affect it on both routes.
  • Covers a missing transaction and calldata whose selector is absent from the supplied interface; both return null.

Why: the regression is an ABI-shape bug. Using generated production interfaces makes the tests validate the actual argument layouts that caused it.

Review verdict + residual findings

Verdict: accept
No blocking issue found for F3. The production path derives the claim position from the parsed fragment, and tests cover both required ABIs plus hash invariants and null cases. git diff --check reported no whitespace errors.

Residual findings

Low — inaccurate route comment
The new JSDoc groups gnosisToArb with the three-argument tuple signature. In the inspected contract, VeaInboxGnosisToArb.sendSnapshot has six scalar inputs and no Claim tuple. The validator’s configured routes here are Arb→Eth and Arb→Gnosis, so this does not block F3, but the comment should not imply broader support.
Low — permissive tuple selection
The helper does not verify that the parsed function is named sendSnapshot or that the tuple has the Claim component shape. Any other successfully parsed function with a tuple would be hashed. Current callers obtain transaction hashes from SnapshotSent records, which limits exposure; explicit name/schema checks would make the helper’s contract tighter.
Low — malformed matching calldata is not covered
The new null-case test uses a selector that the supplied interface cannot match. A known selector with truncated or otherwise undecodable arguments may make ethers throw during parseTransaction; this function does not catch that locally. This is hardening outside the stated two-ABI regression, not a blocker.

Verification note

This report is based on read-only Git inspection of the full diff, caller context, route configuration, and Solidity signatures. The test suite was not executed under the read-only inspection constraint.
